changelog: Paraphrased C3 to be shorter while keeping its warning about unresolved scope in unstable openers (freeing space).

Inserted a new principle immediately after C3 that defines and flags 'continuation heads' (verbs missing objects, prepositions without complements, subordinators/comparatives, quantifiers, auxiliaries) as high‑contra and advises avoiding cuts that leave them on the left — directly addressing the primary finding.

Inserted a new principle after C5 that clarifies the post‑nominal modifier guidance: do not ban internal noun‑group cuts outright; decide whether a modifier is essential, and if keeping it would force breaking predicate–argument integrity or create a continuation head, prefer keeping the predicate+arguments together — addressing the second finding without imposing an absolute prohibition.

Replace C5 to soften the blanket ban on internal noun-group cuts: instruct assessing whether a post-nominal modifier is essential and prefer keeping predicate+arguments together when preserving a modifier would force splitting predicates or create a stranded continuation head — addresses the primary finding.

Replace example E1 with measured example en_us_733 so the prompt shows a real short‑latency case where a stranded continuation head (predicate needing its complement) causes high contradiction risk — addressing the primary finding while obeying the examples_only constraint.

Replace C6 to keep protection for essential post‑nominal modifiers but explicitly allow abandoning modifier preservation when doing so would split predicate–argument structure or leave a continuation head on the left, protecting very short‑latency cases.
